title: Dehumidifier vs. Air Conditioner: Which Fixes Humidity?
h1: Dehumidifier vs. Air Conditioner: Which One Do You Actually Need?
dek: Your AC dries the air only while it’s busy cooling. On mild, muggy days, that’s not enough — here’s how to tell which machine solves your problem.
description: Dehumidifier vs. air conditioner: how much moisture each removes, why AC short-cycling leaves rooms clammy, running costs, and when you need both.
intro: The **dehumidifier vs. air conditioner** question comes up every humid summer, and it’s easy to see why: both are boxy appliances that make a room feel better. But they’re built for different jobs. An air conditioner lowers temperature and removes moisture only as a side effect of cooling. A dehumidifier exists to pull water from the air and does it whatever the temperature.

That difference matters most on the days that feel worst — mild, rainy stretches in spring and fall when it’s not hot enough for the AC to run long, but the air is heavy and damp. The house ends up cool *and* clammy at the same time.
Here’s how much each machine really does for humidity, when your AC quietly falls short, and how to decide which to buy first.
topPicksLead: If humidity is your main complaint, start with a dedicated room dehumidifier like the **Midea Cube 50**; if heat is the problem, a dual-hose portable AC such as the **Whynter ARC-14S** is the better tool.

head: Dehumidifier
Air conditioner
rows: No — stops once the thermostat is satisfied

blocks.text: Both machines use the same basic trick: air passes over a cold coil, water condenses and drips away. The difference is what controls the compressor. An AC follows the thermostat; a dehumidifier follows the humidistat. Our [how a dehumidifier works](/guides/how-does-a-dehumidifier-work/) guide explains the cycle in more detail.

sections.heading: Why your house feels damp with the AC running

blocks.text: An AC only dehumidifies once its coil gets cold enough and stays cold for a while. On a hot afternoon, it runs long cycles and wrings out plenty of water. On a 72°F rainy day, it reaches the thermostat setting in minutes and shuts off — often before much moisture has been removed, and some of what condensed can re-evaporate back into the air. HVAC technicians call this **short-cycling**.
Oversized central systems make it worse, because they cool the house so quickly that they rarely run long enough to dry it. The result is the classic cold-and-clammy feeling.

blocks.title: Does a dehumidifier cool a room?
blocks.text: No — it slightly warms it, because the compressor and fan give off heat. But dry air *feels* cooler, so many people find they can set the thermostat a degree or two higher. More in [does a dehumidifier cool a room?](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-cool-a-room/)

items.label: Choose a dehumidifier if…
items.text: The room is a comfortable temperature but feels sticky, windows fog, or a basement, crawl space or bathroom stays damp year-round.
sub: Musty smells despite the AC running
Mild, rainy weather is when it feels worst

items.label: Choose an air conditioner if…
items.text: Heat is the main complaint and the room is genuinely hot, not just humid.
sub: No central air in that room
Peak summer temperatures are the problem
You need a self-contained unit for one space

items.label: Choose both if…
items.text: The space is hot in summer and damp in the shoulder seasons — common in humid climates and finished basements.

blocks.text: Not sure? Put a hygrometer in the room for a week. If humidity stays high even when the temperature is fine, it’s a dehumidifier problem. Our [when to use a dehumidifier](/guides/when-to-use-a-dehumidifier/) guide lists the warning signs.

sections.heading: How to run an AC and a dehumidifier together

items: Let the AC handle temperature during hot weather, when its long cycles also dry the air.
Run the dehumidifier at 45–50% through mild, damp stretches when the AC barely runs.
Keep the dehumidifier in the dampest area — usually the basement — rather than next to an AC vent.
Once humidity is under control, try raising the thermostat a degree or two; drier air feels cooler.
Close windows while either machine runs, or you’ll be conditioning the outdoors.

blocks.text: An air conditioner and a dehumidifier aren’t rivals — they do different jobs. If a room is damp but already comfortable, buy a dehumidifier. If it’s hot, buy an AC, but don’t count on it to keep humidity in check on mild, rainy days. For basements that stay damp no matter the season, start with our [basement dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) picks.

faqs.q: Will my air conditioner remove humidity on its own?
faqs.a: Some. A central AC can remove roughly 5–20 gallons a day in typical summer conditions, but only while it’s running long cooling cycles. On mild, humid days it short-cycles and removes much less.

faqs.q: Why does my house feel damp even with the AC on?
faqs.a: Usually short-cycling. When it’s mild but humid, the AC hits its temperature target quickly and shuts off before it has dried the air, leaving the house cool and clammy.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to run a dehumidifier or an air conditioner for humidity?
faqs.a: A dehumidifier, if humidity is the only problem. It runs only until the target humidity is reached, while an AC has to run full cooling cycles to dry the air as a side effect. See [how much electricity a dehumidifier uses](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) for estimates.

faqs.q: Can I use a dehumidifier instead of an air conditioner?
faqs.a: Only if temperature isn’t the issue. A dehumidifier doesn’t cool and adds a little heat. It’s the right tool for a damp room that’s already comfortable.

faqs.q: Do I need both a dehumidifier and an air conditioner?
faqs.a: Many humid-climate homes and basements benefit from both: the AC for hot weather and a dehumidifier for damp shoulder seasons and below-grade spaces.

faqs.q: Does an AC’s dry mode replace a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Not fully. Dry or dehumidify modes run the compressor at low fan speed to favor moisture removal, which helps, but a dedicated dehumidifier removes more water per hour and holds a precise humidity setting.
